note: What this build is EXPECTED to conclude for each corpus document. `rows` is the comparison input; every row that is not `agree` must carry a reason in `known`, or the oracle fails (test/oracle/classify.ts unexplainedRows). Re-seeding this file to silence a failure is the thing that gate exists to prevent. All seven non-agreeing rows below were confirmed PRE-EXISTING by replaying the pre-S165 build (87b3f38) over this same corpus: that build scores 16 cardinal FP / 9 lost TP / 41 agree, and every row here is wrong there too.

known.include(child {julia}) then {r} + cache: CARDINAL FP, PRE-EXISTING (wrong in 87b3f38 too). Quarto expands `{{< include >}}` PRE-engine, so it counts the child's {julia} and resolves jupyter; we cannot see the child from the open buffer and answer knitr. S165 measured BOTH options and chose to DECLINE rather than answer "ambiguous", because ambiguity would cost the knitr-only fields on every ordinary include-bearing book chapter — a rare conditional FP against a common lost TP is the reverse of this project's settled trade. BACKLOG: An {{< include >}} makes the document's language set unknowable.
known.nested include(child→grand {julia}) then: CARDINAL FP, PRE-EXISTING. Same root cause as the row above, proving includes RECURSE (doc -> child -> grandchild). Same filed item.
known.execute: {engine: markdown} FLOW + {r} +: CARDINAL FP, PRE-EXISTING. Quarto honours the FLOW spelling `execute: {engine: markdown}` and renders exit 0; neither value enumerator emits a flow-mapping MEMBER, so `documentEngineForScoping` sees nothing to read. S165 made any scalar token on `execute:` UNREADABLE so this declines rather than letting the language fallback squiggle every cell — the FP is unchanged, but it no longer widens. BACKLOG: The FLOW spellings of the engine: override.
known.{r.foo} dotted token + echo: CARDINAL FP, PRE-EXISTING. Quarto's fence recognizer captures `([=A-Za-z]+)`, so `{r.foo}` is not an executable cell to it at all and nothing in it is validated (exit 0); our CELL_INFO tail `[^}]*` admits the `.foo`, so we treat it as an {r} cell and flag the engine-AGNOSTIC `echo`. The knitr-only `cache` half of this pair is already `agree` because the language scan does not count `r.foo` either, so the document resolves to markdown. Same root cause as the filed digit-bearing token item, which does not name the DOTTED spelling. BACKLOG: A digit-bearing fence token is not a cell to quarto at all.
known.include(child {r}) then {python} + cache: LOST TP (safe), PRE-EXISTING. The include decline in the other direction: quarto sees the child's {r}, resolves knitr and rejects (exit 1); we decline and stay silent. The safe half of the same filed trade.
known.REVIEW engine: &a knitr (TP we give up): LOST TP (safe), PRE-EXISTING. We compare a RAW token where quarto resolves the PARSED node, so an anchored `&a knitr` is unreadable to us and we decline. Quarto really does select knitr here (exit 1). Separating this from its exit-0 twins needs real YAML node resolution. BACKLOG: Node-property spellings of the override.
known.REVIEW engine: | + literal body (TP we g: LOST TP (safe), PRE-EXISTING. A literal block scalar KEEPS its newline so quarto reads `markdown\n` and falls through to the languages (exit 1), while the `>-` folded twin strips it and matches (exit 0). Telling them apart needs chomping semantics — exactly the trap S163 filed. Same filed item as the row above.
